import sys, json

# --- per-answer call budget ------------------------------------------------
# One brain answer may carry N calls in ONE bundle. The ITERATION cap lives at
# the seam that starts a round (the collector); the CALL cap lives here,
# because only this cell ever sees the whole bundle.
MAX_CALLS = int("${DISPATCHER_MAX_CALLS:-16}")
# --- the async tool class (GH #28, R-CG-3) ---------------------------------
# Some tools do not answer inside a round. An advisor that THINKS comes back
# minutes later, on a lane of its own -- and a fan-in that waits for it would
# be racing its own idle window instead of ending the turn. Naming such a tool
# HERE is the one declaration: this cell is the only one that ever sees the
# whole bundle, so it is the only one that can classify a call. The call still
# travels the ordinary way; what travels with it is the marker.
ASYNC_TOOLS = set(x.strip() for x in "${DISPATCHER_ASYNC_TOOLS:-}".split(",") if x.strip())
# --- the handoff class (GH #372) -------------------------------------------
# A STRONGER form of async, and the difference is the turn: an async call does
# not answer inside the round; a HANDOFF call takes the turn with it, because
# the answer will come from a later turn -- an advisor's event arriving on its
# own lane, an escalation re-entering the seam as a fresh assembly. The round it
# leaves behind is therefore over even when no sentence stood beside it.
#
# Everything else in the async class is fire-and-forget: `remember` writes and
# never comes back, and the model still owes THIS turn an answer. Told apart
# nowhere else, a bundle of one bare `remember` call ended the turn in silence --
# no interim, no final, no error (measured: three of five harness runs). Which
# of the two a tool is, is tool semantics, so it is DECLARED, in the one cell
# that sees the whole bundle and already classifies. A handoff tool is async by
# definition, so naming it here is enough -- the union below is the whole of it.
HANDOFF_TOOLS = set(x.strip() for x in "${DISPATCHER_HANDOFF_TOOLS:-}".split(",") if x.strip())
ASYNC_TOOLS |= HANDOFF_TOOLS

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
# --- the interim class (GH #539) -------------------------------------------
# A sentence standing beside a bundle is an INTERIM answer, and interim is a
# promise made to a CHANNEL: the user reads this now, the real answer follows.
# A brain WITHOUT a channel has nowhere to put such a sentence. An advisor
# core's answer lane IS the advice lane of the voice that asked it, so an
# interim arriving there is filed as the advice it is not -- and the voice
# verbalises it, and sometimes asks again, and the core answers with the next
# interim (measured on a live colony: 11 of 26 answers one core put on that
# lane were interim, and all 11 arrived as advice).
#
# Whether the brain behind this cell has a channel cannot be read off a bundle,
# so it is DECLARED -- in the same cell that already declares the async and the
# handoff class, for the same reason: this is the only cell that sees the whole
# bundle, and a sentence beside it is part of that bundle. Default ON, so every
# wiring that exists keeps the behaviour it has. It reads from `params`, not
# from a fourth environment token, because that is the direction the knobs are
# moving (GH #138).
P = doc.get("params") or {}
_interim = P.get("interim", "1")
INTERIM = str("1" if _interim is None else _interim).strip().lower() \
    not in ("", "0", "false", "no")
hop = (envelope.get("header") or {}).get("hop") or {}
finish = str(hop.get("finish_reason", "") or "")
msgs = d.get("messages", [])
calls = [m for m in msgs if m.get("type") == "tool_call"]


def emit(out):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))
    sys.exit(0)


def error_result(call_id, text, code):
    """A synthetic tool_result in place of a call that will never run. It keeps
    the original tool_call_id, so the round stays fan-in-complete: the brain
    sees the failure and has to answer it instead of waiting for it. Dropping
    the call silently would stall the fan-in until the TTL runs out, and TTL
    expiry emits nothing at all towards the surface."""
    return {"header": {"route": "result", "tool_call_id": call_id, "error_code": code},
            "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": call_id,
                          "text": text}]}


def parts_of(call, i):
    """(id, name, raw arguments) of one OpenAI-form tool_call turn, whose text
    is the stringified function object. `name` is None when the turn cannot be
    read that way -- an unroutable call, not a tool."""
    call_id = str(call.get("id") or "call-%d" % i)
    try:
        fn = json.loads(call.get("text") or "{}")
    except Exception:
        return call_id, None, None
    if not isinstance(fn, dict) or not fn.get("name"):
        return call_id, None, None
    args = fn.get("arguments", "{}")
    if not isinstance(args, str):
        args = json.dumps(args)
    return call_id, str(fn["name"]), args


def async_keys(call_id, args):
    """The hop keys an async call carries. `consult_id` correlates the whole
    exchange: a FRESH consult is named by the call that opened it, a REPLY to a
    question the advisor asked back passes the id it was shown -- so the
    advisor keeps one thread instead of guessing which of its questions was
    answered. `consult_eta` is the model's own coarse duration estimate,
    produced in the SAME turn (GH #123): it is logged and nothing reads it."""
    try:
        a = json.loads(args or "{}")
    except Exception:
        a = {}
    if not isinstance(a, dict):
        a = {}
    return {"async": "1", "consult_id": str(a.get("consult_id") or call_id),
            "consult_eta": str(a.get("eta", "") or "")}


if not calls:
    # No bundle. The final answer travels; anything else stops here. The llm
    # error path echoes the INPUT conversation back with finish_reason "error",
    # and putting that on the answer lane would file the prompt as the agent's
    # own words -- an error lane belongs on the brain's edge, not in this cell.
    if finish == "stop":
        emit([{"header": {"route": "answer", "finish_reason": finish}, "messages": msgs}])
    emit([])

parsed = [parts_of(c, i) for i, c in enumerate(calls)]
async_ids = [cid for cid, name, _ in parsed if name in ASYNC_TOOLS]
handoff_ids = [cid for cid, name, _ in parsed if name in HANDOFF_TOOLS]

# PLAIN order: the expectation set FIRST, the calls after it. A tool that
# answers instantly must not reach the fan-in before the round exists there.
# `async_calls` rides on the same message: the fan-in is TOLD which ids it must
# not wait for, instead of keeping a second copy of the classification.
# `handoff_calls` rides beside `async_calls` and is always present, empty
# included: a hop key that is sometimes absent makes a CEL modifier fail, and a
# failed modifier skips the edge.
out = [{"header": {"route": "calls", "call_count": str(len(calls)),
                   "async_calls": ",".join(async_ids),
                   "handoff_calls": ",".join(handoff_ids)}, "messages": msgs}]

# Content AND tool_calls out of ONE response (R-CG-3, delta 1): a sentence next
# to the bundle belongs in the channel now, and the turn ends with it while the
# calls keep running. Asking a second inference for "one moment" is exactly the
# extra turn the advisor split abolishes.
#
# WHETHER IT IS INTERIM DEPENDS ON THE BUNDLE BESIDE IT (GH #378). This used to
# be marked `interim` unconditionally, and that stranded every turn of the
# shape an async tool description asks for -- 10 of 12 measured rounds under the
# shipped contract. `interim` is a promise that a final answer follows, so it is
# only true when something is still coming:
#
#   a NON-ASYNC call     the round re-enters the brain with its result, so a
#                        further answer is on its way        -> interim
#   a HANDOFF call       takes the turn with it; the answer arrives as a later
#                        turn                                -> interim
#   async, no handoff    fire-and-forget, and the model still owes THIS turn an
#                        answer -- the sentence IS it        -> FINAL
#
# So the sentence is final exactly when every call is async-and-not-handoff.
# That is the precise mirror of the fan-in's `acked and not waiting and over`:
# it files such a round as fired and never re-enters, which is correct -- what
# was wrong is that the only thing delivered had been labelled interim, so the
# turn carried an interim answer and no final one, forever.
said = [m for m in msgs
        if m.get("type") in ("text", None) and str(m.get("text", "") or "")]
if said:
    waited_for = [cid for cid, _, _ in parsed
                  if cid not in async_ids or cid in handoff_ids]
    header = {"route": "answer", "finish_reason": finish}
    if waited_for:
        header["interim"] = "1"
    # AND ONLY IF THERE IS SOMEWHERE TO SAY IT (GH #539). `INTERIM` off means
    # the brain behind this cell has no channel, and then the sentence does not
    # leave this cell at all -- not on the answer lane, and so not into the
    # window either, because the `calls` lane hands the fan-in the assistant
    # turn and the fan-in drops its text on the ground that the answer lane
    # wrote it. Both halves say the same thing: a sentence nobody could hear
    # was never said. The FINAL sentence still leaves whatever the knob says --
    # `waited_for` empty is the GH #378 case, where nothing is coming after it
    # and the sentence IS the answer this turn owes. What is withheld is only
    # the PROMISE of a later one, and a promise nobody can read is not one.
    if INTERIM or not waited_for:
        out.append({"header": header, "messages": said})

if len(calls) > MAX_CALLS:
    reason = "call budget exceeded: %d calls in one answer, limit %d" % (len(calls), MAX_CALLS)
    for call_id, _, _ in parsed:
        out.append(error_result(call_id, reason, "call_budget_exceeded"))
    emit(out)

for call_id, name, args in parsed:
    if name is None:
        out.append(error_result(call_id,
                                "malformed tool_call: text is not a JSON object with a name",
                                "malformed_tool_call"))
        continue
    # No topology knowledge: this cell names the TOOL, an edge knows the CELL.
    header = {"route": "tool", "tool_name": name, "tool_call_id": call_id}
    if name in ASYNC_TOOLS:
        header.update(async_keys(call_id, args))
    out.append({"header": header,
                "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": call_id,
                              "text": args}]})
emit(out)

max_calls.description: Per-answer call budget (DISPATCHER_MAX_CALLS): how many tool calls one brain answer may fan out. A bundle above the budget runs NO tool; every expected call is answered with a synthetic error tool_result instead, so the round stays fan-in-complete. The iteration cap of the loop is a different knob and lives at the seam that starts a round.

async_tools.description: Comma-separated names of tools that do NOT answer inside a round (DISPATCHER_ASYNC_TOOLS, GH #28). This is the ONE place the async class is declared: the dispatcher is the only cell that sees the whole bundle, so it classifies, and it names the affected tool_call_ids in hop.async_calls on the calls lane - the fan-in opens no expectation for them and therefore never races an idle window against thinking time. An async call otherwise travels like any other tool call, plus hop.async, hop.consult_id (arguments.consult_id when the model answers an open question, the tool_call_id when it opens a new one) and hop.consult_eta (the model's own coarse duration estimate, observe-only).

handoff_tools.description: Comma-separated names of tools whose call ENDS the turn (DISPATCHER_HANDOFF_TOOLS, GH #372). A handoff is the stronger form of the async class: the call does not answer inside the round AND the answer will come from a LATER turn - an advisor's event on its own lane, an escalation re-entering the seam as a fresh assembly - so the round it leaves behind is over even when no sentence stood beside it. Naming a tool here declares it async as well; the two lists are unioned. Everything else in the async class is fire-and-forget (a memory write): the model still owes THIS turn an answer, and a bundle that is nothing but such a call re-enters the brain for the iteration it has not spent instead of ending the turn in silence. The ids leave on hop.handoff_calls beside hop.async_calls.

interim.description: Whether a sentence standing NEXT to a tool bundle leaves as an interim answer (params surface, GH #539). `interim` is a promise made to a CHANNEL - the user reads this sentence now, the real answer follows - so it is only true where a channel exists. An advisor core has none: its answer lane is the ADVICE lane of the voice that asked, and an interim arriving there is filed as an advice, verbalised, and sometimes answered with a fresh consultation, which the core answers with the next interim. Off (`""`, `0`, `false`, `no`) the sentence does not leave this cell at all, and therefore does not enter the brain's own window either - a sentence nobody could hear was never said. A FINAL sentence is not affected: where nothing is waited for, the sentence IS the answer of the turn (GH #378) and leaves whatever this knob says. Default on, so every wiring that exists keeps its behaviour; a brain without a channel turns it off.

description.purpose: Fan-OUT of one brain answer: it splits a bundle of tool_calls into one message per call, lets a sentence that stands NEXT to the bundle leave as an interim answer in the same response -- where there is a channel to say it in (`interim`, GH #539) -- and lets a final answer through. The assistant turn goes to the fan-in first (route 'calls'), then each call leaves with hop.tool_name and hop.tool_call_id and nothing else -- which cell that name belongs to is decided by an edge, so the split works in any topology. Tools named in DISPATCHER_ASYNC_TOOLS are classified here as the async class: their ids ride on hop.async_calls, and the fan-in opens no expectation for them. DISPATCHER_HANDOFF_TOOLS is the stronger class on top of it (GH #372): a handoff call takes the TURN with it because the answer comes from a later turn, so the round it leaves behind is over even without a sentence beside it - its ids ride on hop.handoff_calls, and an async call that is NOT a handoff leaves the round to be answered. The `interim` knob is the third declaration of the same kind and the only one on the params surface (GH #138): whether the brain behind this cell has a CHANNEL, which no bundle shows. Off, a sentence beside a bundle that is still being waited for does not leave this cell -- an advisor core's answer lane is the advice lane of the voice that asked it, and an interim filed there is an advice nobody gave.
description.use_when: Directly behind an agent's llm cell, in front of the tool cells and the collector's in_calls / in_tool / in_answer ports. One per brain. Wire the async class when a tool answers on a lane of its own instead of inside the round (an advisor core, a long errand), and the handoff class on top of it when that lane also takes the turn over (an advisor whose event opens a fresh round, an escalation) - a fire-and-forget write is async and NOT a handoff. Turn `interim` off where the brain has no channel -- an advisor core, anything whose answer lane feeds another agent rather than a user (GH #539).
description.not_in_scope: No fan-IN (that is the collector's: expectation sets, round completeness, re-entry) - the dispatcher CLASSIFIES a call and the collector obeys the marker, which is why both the async and the handoff class are declared here and read there. No tool execution, no argument validation, no knowledge of which tools exist. No iteration counting and no restore_ttl: the loop is bounded on the re-entry edge, not here. No error routing for a failed inference -- a turn that is neither a bundle nor a final answer is terminal. No consumer for hop.consult_eta: the duration estimate is carried and logged, never acted on (GH #123, observe-only). And no knowledge of WHERE an answer goes: the `interim` knob says whether a channel exists, never which one -- the lane is an edge's business as it always was.
description.emits_meaning: route 'calls': the assistant turn verbatim, the expectation set of the round, ALWAYS first (PLAIN order); hop.call_count sizes it, hop.async_calls names the ids the fan-in must NOT wait for, and hop.handoff_calls names the subset of those whose call ends the turn (GH #372) - both keys always travel, empty included. route 'answer' with hop.interim=1: the text turn(s) that stood next to the bundle, on their way to the channel while the calls keep running -- the turn ends with this sentence, no second inference is needed for it. With `interim` off there is no channel and this emission does not happen at all (GH #539); the FINAL sentence below is unaffected. route 'tool': one call, hop.tool_name for the edge condition, hop.tool_call_id for the fan-in, body = one tool_call turn carrying the RAW arguments; an async call carries hop.async=1, hop.consult_id (the correlation of the whole exchange - the tool_call_id for a fresh consult, arguments.consult_id when the model answers a question the advisor asked back) and hop.consult_eta (arguments.eta, the model's own coarse estimate). route 'result': a synthetic error tool_result for a call that will never run (budget exceeded, or a call that cannot be read), hop.error_code names which, and the tool_call_id is preserved so the round stays complete. route 'answer' without hop.interim: the brain's final turn, passed through with hop.finish_reason. A turn that is neither a bundle nor a final answer emits NOTHING (empty multi-send, terminal by design).
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: the assistant turn as the llm cell emits it -- tool_call turns whose text is the stringified OpenAI function object ({name, arguments}), a text turn, or both. hop.finish_reason: 'stop' releases the answer; a bundle of tool_calls is dispatched whatever the finish reason says.
examples: 2 calls -> 3 emissions: calls(the assistant turn) , tool{tool_name: web_search, tool_call_id: c1}, tool{tool_name: web_fetch, tool_call_id: c2}

1 NON-async call plus a sentence -> 3 emissions: calls(both turns), answer{interim: 1} with the sentence alone, tool{...}; with an async non-handoff call instead, the same sentence goes out with NO interim key -- nothing is being waited for, so it IS the answer (GH #378)

DISPATCHER_HANDOFF_TOOLS=consult_cogny, a consult call c1 next to a web_search c2 -> hop.async_calls='c1' AND hop.handoff_calls='c1' on the calls lane (a handoff declares itself async); the consult leaves with async=1, consult_id=c1 and consult_eta from arguments.eta, the search leaves unmarked
a consult call whose arguments carry {consult_id: 'k-7'} -> hop.consult_id='k-7' while hop.tool_call_id stays the call's own id: the advisor keeps one thread across question and answer
17 calls with DISPATCHER_MAX_CALLS=16 -> 18 emissions: calls + 17 results 'call budget exceeded', no tool runs and no id is lost
finish_reason stop -> 1 emission on route 'answer', the turn unchanged

DISPATCHER_HANDOFF_TOOLS=escalate_to_deep, a bare escalation call with no text -> hop.async_calls='e1' AND hop.handoff_calls='e1': the fan-in files the round as over, because the answer comes from the turn the escalation opens

the same bundle for a fire-and-forget `remember` (async, NOT a handoff) -> hop.handoff_calls='' and the fan-in leaves the round open, so the brain gets the iteration it has not spent instead of the channel getting nothing (GH #372)

`interim` off (an advisor core) with the same 1 NON-async call plus a sentence -> 2 emissions: calls(both turns) and tool{...}, and NOTHING on the answer lane; the core's ONE final answer, a round later, still leaves as the single advice the asking voice waited for

`interim` off and a bare async non-handoff call plus a sentence -> the sentence STILL leaves on route 'answer' without hop.interim: nothing is waited for, so it is the final answer of the turn (GH #378) and the knob does not touch it
